questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to set up a local, secure package mirror with an unprivileged worker, automated scheduling, proper web serving, and log maintenance—core RHCSA skills.

## Key Concepts
- reposync usage and local mirror layout
- systemd service and timer for automation
- httpd configuration and permissions
- GPG verification and key management
- logrotate for auditability and disk health

## Code Example
```bash
# Example systemd service (reposync.service)
[Unit]
Description=Populate local Yum mirror
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
User=reposync
ExecStart=/usr/bin/reposync -p /var/www/html/repos -r base -n
StandardOutput=journal
StandardError=journal
```

```bash
# Example systemd timer (reposync.timer)
[Unit]
Description=Daily reposync for local mirror
Requires=reposync.service

[Timer]
OnCalendar=daily
Persistent=true

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
```

```bash
# Example httpd config snippet
Alias /repos /var/www/html/repos
<Directory /var/www/html/repos>
    Options Indexes FollowSymLinks
    AllowOverride None
    Require all granted
    EnableSendfile on
</Directory>
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate the mirror serves content correctly?
- How would you add a second repo and handle multiple architectures?

## Why This Is Asked
Assesses practical LVM thin provisioning, snapshot lifecycle, and automation on RHEL 9. Tests naming discipline, space planning, and safe pruning without downtime.

## Key Concepts
- LVM thin provisioning across multiple PVs
- Thin pool and thin LV creation syntax
- Systemd timer-based automation
- Snapshot retention and safe deletion
- Validation via lvdisplay and /dev/mapper

## Code Example
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# prune-thin-snapshots.sh
cutoff=$(date -d '7 days ago' +%s)
for snap in /dev/data-vg/data-snap-*; do
  [ -e "$snap" ] || continue
  dateStr=${snap##*-}
  snapTs=$(date -d "$dateStr" +%s 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  if [ "$snapTs" -lt "$cutoff" ]; then
    lvremove -y "$snap" >/dev/null 2>&1
  fi
done
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test recovery if the thin pool fills up?
- How would you monitor snapshot usage and alert on pruning failures?

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical knowledge of file integrity monitoring, systemd timers, on-demand triggers, and rollback procedures at the RHCSA level.

## Key Concepts
- AIDE baseline creation and verification
- systemd timers and services for scheduled checks
- inotify-based triggers for immediate rechecks
- Rollback strategies for baseline databases
- auditd integration for baseline-change logging

## Code Example
```bash
# Install and initialize baseline
sudo dnf install -y aide
sudo aide --init
sudo mv /var/lib/aide/aide.db.new.gz /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz

# Backup baseline with timestamp
sudo cp /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz.$(date +%Y%m%d)

# Create systemd service for daily checks
sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/aide-check.service <<EOF
[Unit]
Description=AIDE Integrity Check

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/sbin/aide --check
EOF

# Create systemd timer for daily execution
sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/aide.timer <<EOF
[Unit]
Description=Daily AIDE Integrity Check Timer

[Timer]
OnCalendar=daily
Persistent=true

[Install]
wantedBy=timers.target
EOF

# Enable and start the timer
sudo systemctl enable --now aide.timer

# Create inotifywait watcher for on-demand rechecks
#!/bin/bash
inotifywait -m -r -e modify,create,delete /etc |
  while read path action file; do
    logger "AIDE: Change detected in /etc - triggering on-demand check"
    /usr/sbin/aide --check
  done
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical mastery of live data migration, LVM, and SELinux in a production-like scenario without downtime.

## Key Concepts

- LVM: create, format, and swap a data volume atomically
- Filesystem: XFS best for large dirs and rapid mounting
- Live migration: rsync with proper flags to preserve metadata
- Persistence: fstab, SELinux labeling, and service health verification

## Code Example

```bash
lvcreate -L500G -n appvar vg0
mkfs.xfs /dev/vg0/appvar
mkdir -p /mnt/appvar /var/www/app
mount /dev/vg0/appvar /mnt/appvar
rsync -aHAX /var/www/app/ /mnt/appvar/
umount /dev/vg0/appvar /var/www/app
echo '/dev/vg0/appvar /var/www/app xfs defaults 0 0' >> /etc/fstab
restorecon -R /var/www/app
```

```javascript
# /etc/rsyslog.d/60-forward.conf (illustrative)
$DefaultNetstreamDriver gtls
$ActionSendStreamDriver gtls
$TLSCACertificateFile /etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt
$TLSCertificateFile /etc/pki/tls/certs/rsyslog-client.crt
$TLSKeyFile /etc/pki/tls/private/rsyslog-client.key
$ActionSendStreamDriverAuthMode x509/name

# Disk-backed queue configuration
$ActionQueueFileName fwdq1
$ActionQueueMaxDiskSpace 1g
$ActionQueuePersistencyInterval 600
$ActionQueueTimeoutEnqueue 86400
$ActionQueueSaveOnShutdown on

# Forward all application logs
*.* @@loghub.example.com:10514
```

```bash
# Test configuration syntax
rsyslogd -N1 -f /etc/rsyslog.conf

# Send test log entry
logger "Test TLS forward to loghub.example.com"

# Verify queue status
ls -la /var/spool/rsyslog/

mv /etc/rsyslog.d/60-forward.conf /etc/rsyslog.d/60-forward.conf.disabled
systemctl restart rsyslog
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests hands-on SSH hardening in RHCSA-style tasks, ensuring secure key-based authentication, proper file permissions, and correct access controls.

## Key Concepts
- SSH daemon hardening (sshd_config)
- Public key authentication, authorized_keys perms
- User permissions and home directory security
- Service management (systemctl restart sshd)

## Code Example
```bash
# as root or user with sudo
mkdir -p /home/deploy/.ssh
chmod 700 /home/deploy/.ssh
ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 4096 -f /home/deploy/.ssh/id_rsa -N '' -C 'deploy@host'
cat /home/deploy/.ssh/id_rsa.pub >> /home/deploy/.ssh/authorized_keys
chmod 600 /home/deploy/.ssh/authorized_keys
sed -i 's/^#*PasswordAuthentication.*/PasswordAuthentication no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config
sed -i 's/^#*PermitRootLogin.*/PermitRootLogin no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config
systemctl restart sshd
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you recover if you lose the deploy private key?
- What additional controls would you add for auditing SSH access?
